concerns.text: Constitution Principle V (Versioning) is mislabeled. The plan text describes 'generating content hashes' and 'updating timestamps', which corresponds to Principle V in the Constitution (Versioning Discipline). However, the plan labels this as 'Principle V (Versioning)' while the Constitution lists 'Principle V' as 'Versioning Discipline' and 'Principle IV' as 'Single Source of Truth'. The plan's mapping of 'Principle IV' to 'Single Source of Truth' is correct, but the plan's 'Principle V' description matches the Constitution's 'Principle V'. The concern is that the plan's 'Principle V' text ('generating content hashes...') is actually describing the Constitution's Principle V, but the plan's 'Principle IV' text ('The data-model.md defines strict schemas...') is describing the Constitution's Principle IV. The plan's numbering is consistent with the Constitution, but the description for Principle V in the plan ('Versioning') is slightly abbreviated compared to the Constitution ('Versioning Discipline'). This is a minor writing issue, but the real issue is the missing mapping for Principle II (Verified Accuracy) in the plan's Constitution Check section. The plan mentions 'Reference-Validator gate' in Principle II, but the Constitution's Principle II is 'Verified Accuracy'. The plan's description for Principle II is 'Citations in research.md will be restricted to the "Verified datasets" block...'. This is a partial match but lacks the explicit mention of the 'Reference-Validator Agent' and the 'Title-token-overlap' threshold required by the Constitution. This is a requirement-level gap because the plan does not fully implement the Constitution's Principle II.

Constitution Principle II (Verified Accuracy) is not fully addressed. The plan states 'Citations in research.md will be restricted to the "Verified datasets" block provided in the prompt. The Reference-Validator gate is acknowledged as a blocking step for artifact transitions.' However, the Constitution's Principle II requires 'Every external citation... MUST be verified by the Reference-Validator Agent against the primary source before contributing review points. Title-token-overlap with the cited source MUST be ≥ CITATION_TITLE_OVERLAP_THRESHOLD (default 0.7).' The plan's description is vague and does not explicitly commit to the 'Title-token-overlap' threshold or the 'Reference-Validator Agent' as the mechanism. This is a requirement-level gap because the plan does not fully implement the Constitution's Principle II.

Constitution Principle V (Versioning) description in the plan is abbreviated. The plan says 'The plan includes generating content hashes for data and model artifacts, updating the project state updated_at timestamp upon completion.' The Constitution's Principle V is 'Versioning Discipline' and requires 'Every artifact under this project carries a content hash. The Advancement-Evaluator Agent invalidates stale review records when the hashed artifact changes. Every research-stage artifact change updates this project's state/projects/PROJ-415-predicting-the-impact-of-alloying-on-the.yaml updated_at timestamp.' The plan's description is a subset of the Constitution's requirement but misses the 'Advancement-Evaluator Agent' role and the 'invalidates stale review records' clause. This is a writing-level issue as the plan is incomplete but not contradictory.

Constitution Principle VII (Descriptor Consistency) in the plan mentions 'pinned mendeleev library' but the Constitution's Principle VII requires 'All atomic descriptors... MUST be computed using fixed, versioned periodic table constants. The Pauling scale for electronegativity MUST be used consistently across all solutes to prevent feature drift.' The plan's description is a partial match but does not explicitly mention the 'Pauling scale' or the 'fixed, versioned periodic table constants' requirement. This is a writing-level issue as the plan is incomplete but not contradictory.

Constitution Principle III (Data Hygiene) in the plan mentions 'Raw data is preserved; transformations produce new files with provenance records (data/curated/data_provenance.json).' The Constitution's Principle III requires 'Datasets MUST be checksummed and the checksum recorded under data/. No data may be modified in place; every transformation MUST produce a new file with a documented derivation. Personally identifying information MUST NOT appear in committed data.' The plan's description is a partial match but misses the 'checksummed' requirement and the 'PII scan' requirement. This is a requirement-level gap because the plan does not fully implement the Constitution's Principle III.

Constitution Principle I (Reproducibility) in the plan mentions 'pinned requirements.txt, fixed random seeds in code/, and checksumming of all data/ artifacts.' The Constitution's Principle I requires 'Every result reported in this project MUST be reproducible by re-running the project's code/ against the project's data/ on a fresh GitHub Actions runner. Random seeds MUST be pinned in code/. External datasets MUST be fetched from the same canonical source on every run.' The plan's description is a partial match but misses the 'fresh GitHub Actions runner' and 'canonical source' requirements. This is a writing-level issue as the plan is incomplete but not contradictory.

Constitution Principle VI (Computational Resource Compliance) in the plan mentions 'CPU-first (scikit-learn). Hyperparameter tuning is limited to a small grid (max_depth 3-10, n_estimators 50-200) to ensure completion within 2 CPU-hours and <7 GB RAM.' The Constitution's Principle VI requires 'All training pipelines MUST complete within the 6-hour GitHub Actions runner limit specified in the feasibility check; model training MUST remain under 2 CPU-hours; dataset size MUST remain under 10 MB to ensure reproducibility within CI constraints.' The plan's description is a partial match but misses the '6-hour GitHub Actions runner limit' and 'dataset size MUST remain under 10 MB' requirements. This is a writing-level issue as the plan is incomplete but not contradictory.

Constitution Principle IV (Single Source of Truth) in the plan mentions 'The data-model.md defines strict schemas. All figures and statistics in the final output will trace back to the data/curated/filtered.csv and the specific model artifacts saved in models/.' The Constitution's Principle IV requires 'Every figure, statistic, or interpretation in the paper MUST trace back to exactly one row in this project's data/ and one block in this project's code/. Derived numbers MUST NOT be hand-typed into the paper.' The plan's description is a partial match but misses the 'one block in this project's code/' and 'Derived numbers MUST NOT be hand-typed into the paper' requirements. This is a writing-level issue as the plan is incomplete but not contradictory.
